q: Question 18 Marks for correct response: 1.00 Negative marking: 0.00 A router receives a packet with a TTL of 1. The router discards it and sends a response back to the sender. What kind of response is this? Marks awarded 0 Difficulty - Attempt% 70 Correct% 30 Your time 1 Avg time 26 When a router receives a packet with a TTL (Time to Live) value of 1, the TTL is decremented to 0, indicating the packet's lifetime has expired. The router discards the packet to prevent it from looping indefinitely. It then sends an ICMP Time Exceeded message (Type 11, Code 0) back to the sender to notify that the packet was discarded due to TTL expiration. This behavior helps diagnose routing issues and is used by tools like traceroute to map network paths

Question 19 Marks for correct response: 1.00 Negative marking: 0.00 Two routers using OSPF exchange updates. One router goes down, then comes back online. Immediately, it floods LSAs. Other routers accept updates, but for a short time, packets are dropped. Why? Marks awarded 0 Difficulty - Attempt% 68 Correct% 40 Your time 1 Avg time 33 When a router using OSPF comes back online and floods Link State Advertisements (LSAs), other routers accept the updates to rebuild their link-state databases. However, routing convergence takes some time since all routers must recalculate shortest path trees (SPF algorithm) and update their routing and forwarding tables. During this convergence period, the forwarding information base (FIB) is inconsistent or incomplete, causing some packets to be dropped temporarily. This delay before the network fully stabilizes is known as routing table convergence del
